newsitem.title: USA: Cook County, Ill., board approves $2.2 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Cook County, Ill., board approves $2.2 bln budget.

text.p: The Cook County, Ill., Board of Commissioners approved a $2.2 billion fiscal 1997 budget late Friday that includes a package of tax hikes and new taxes to raise $38 million to $40 million.
"Finding alternative sources of revenues was of paramount inportance and those changes in funding are reflected in this budget," said County Board President John Stroger in a news release.
Stroger proposed the budget earlier this month, saying it laid the groundwork for eliminating a structural budget deficit that could reach $850 million by 2000.

During a marathon meeting Friday, County commissioners approved a two cent hike in the county's cigarette tax, subjected diesel fuel users to the same charges as gasoline users, instituted a three percent ticket tax for concerts and other events, and created a service fee for the county courts.

The budget included no new debt issuance for the fiscal year that begins Dec. 1. However, commissioners are expected to vote next month on the sale of about $70 million of tender notes to finance the acquisition and renovation of a downtown Chicago office building for county use, according to Thomas Glaser, the county's chief financial officer.
He said J.P. Morgan Securities would be the senior manager on the deal, with Reinoso & Co. as the co-senior. Glaser added the notes would eventually be replaced with long-term bonds.

Cook County officials have also been eyeing the possibility of refunding $250 million of outstanding general obligation debt. In addition, the county has embarked on a plan to replace its public hospital with a new $500 million-plus facility.
Stroger said plans for the hospital were "on time, on target and on budget," adding that a groundbreaking should be held next fall.

The county sold $114 million of general obligation bonds in July as part of a larger bond issue to get the hospital project started. Glaser has said that no further debt sales are planned for the project until 1998. --Karen Pierog, 312-408-8647
